thread:
tariq: quick q — our Go SSE client is occasionally throwing JSON decode errors when auth refresh happens mid-stream. looks like we get half a chunk then reconnect and the incremental decoder chokes. anyone seen this pattern?

jess: yep seen that. are you using the stdlib decoder (json.Decoder) with a bufio.Reader? that usually handles streaming ndjson fine but partial chunks from reconnects are the tricky bit.

sam: can you paste the chunk boundary? sometimes SSE "data: " framing helps. if the server sends full `data: {...}\n\n` frames it should be ok. partial or split JSON inside a single `data:` is the problem.

tariq: repro snippet: we receive something like `data: {"id":1,"text":"hello` then reconnect, next connection gives ` world"}` and the decoder errors with "unexpected EOF".

```go
r := bufio.NewReader(conn)
d := json.NewDecoder(r)
for d.More() {
  var ev Event
  if err := d.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
    log.Printf("decode err: %v", err)
    // we currently retry the whole request, but downstream app sees a corrupt partial event
  }
}
```

nyla: two angles: server-side framing (send each event as complete ndjson line), and client-side incremental assemble. Go's Decoder expects complete JSON token boundaries. If reconnect happens you need to treat partial buffers as stateful — store trailing bytes and prepend to next stream before decode.

jess: +1. Another approach: treat SSE `data:` lines as atomic strings and only run json.Unmarshal on the concatenated data lines for a single SSE event. i.e., do your own line parser that respects SSE event boundaries instead of using json.Decoder on the raw socket.

sam: also watch backpressure — if your consumer is slow, net.Conn.Read might give very small chunks (multibyte chars cut), which looks like partial JSON even without reconnects. using a larger internal buffer and a non-blocking assembler helps.

tariq: hmm, we do use the SSE framing but currently pass the whole conn into the Decoder. switching to a per-event parse seems safe. any common utility code we should borrow?

jess: we have a small helper in devex utils: `sse/reader.go` — it yields complete `data` payload strings. not sure if it's published yet. @eng-bot can you link the snippet?

eng-bot: snippet: https://stash.internal/redwood/devex/sse-utils/reader.go (perm: eng+devex) :robot_face:

nyla: for retries/dup handling — add an idempotency field to events (if not already) so if you re-process after a reconnect you can dedupe. also ensure retries use backoff so you don't hammer the server while it's healing.

sam: Go-specific tip: use `bytes.Buffer` to accumulate partial JSON bytes and only call `json.Unmarshal` when you detect the full event end (SSE double-newline). Avoid `Decoder` directly on the socket unless server guarantees token boundaries.

tariq: thanks — plan: update client to 1) parse SSE `data:` events into whole strings 2) append trailing partials to buffer across reconnects 3) add idempotency checks on event id 4) exponential backoff on retries. i'll send a PR.

jess: sounds good. when you have a PR ping me for a quick review. also add a test that injects split multibyte Unicode across chunks — that was a gotcha for the Python client previously.

tariq: noted. one more: are there recommended headers for graceful reconnects? we currently send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and when refresh occurs we 401 then reopen. any header to suggest resume?

sam: SSE doesn't have a built-in resume. some implementations use `Last-Event-ID` header (or `id` field in event plus `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect) — server can skip already-sent events. if you can, include an `event_id` in payload and set `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect.

nyla: also check token refresh timing — prefer refreshing proactively (short TTL window) so you don't hit mid-stream 401s. or implement graceful retry: if you get 401, pause consumer, refresh, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`.

tariq: perfect. i'll prototype and include a small go test that simulates partial frames + a mid-stream 401. will ping here with the PR link. thanks all :thumbsup:

jess: awesome — thanks for filing this. if you want, we can add a short doc to devex about SSE best-practices (go/python/js patterns).
